_comment: Controlled vocabulary for question-bank and lesson metadata. Extend by adding new values here first — never invent a skill/representation label inline inside a content or question-bank file. `build/validate.js` fails the build on any value not listed here. Note: `objective` is the C-prefixed cluster id (e.g. "C2.5", from the unit architecture §2) and `cedTopic` is the College Board CED topic number (e.g. "2.5"); both are required on every item and lesson.

courses._comment: Course-reuse index. Every question, lesson, and topic carries a `courses` array listing every course it can be used in as-is. The build/filter for a given course includes only items whose `courses` contains that course. This replaces the retired `apIbConnection` field: materials are tagged by where they can be reused, not by exam-framework code. An item shared across AP and IB gets multiple values; the pedagogical reasoning type lives in `skill`/`representation`/`cognitiveLevel`, which are already course-neutral.

difficulty._source: rigor-standard-addendum.md §21 — canonical, do not modify without updating that document

skill._comment: Seeded with the skills needed for the Unit 2 Dynamics prototype. Add more as new units are authored.

misconception._comment: Controlled vocabulary for the CONCEPT-INVENTORY `misconception` field (architecture §6 / §10.3). build/validate.js warns when a concept-inventory item uses a slug not listed here. `newtonian-anchor` tags a baseline (no-misconception) item. Bank items' free-form `misconceptionTested` (the specific wrong reasoning a distractor encodes) is intentionally NOT constrained to this list.

conceptInventoryItemFields._comment: Extra schema fields a concept-inventory item carries beyond the standard question schema (architecture §10.4). `objective`/`cedTopic`/`clusterId` point at the cluster the correct answer turns on (for internal per-cluster analysis, never shown to students).

lessonThreeTier._source: rigor-standard-addendum.md §3 — page-layout grouping only, maps onto the difficulty scale above
